summary: Francis Louis Noël Goré worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the Séminaire des Missions Étrangères de Paris (~1903–1905) and College General (~1905–1907), later serving as vicaire apostolique and procureur with the Tibet Mission (1931–1952).

Francis N. J. is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned a Master's in Ancient History at the University of Calicut and completed his doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

Francis Vincent Tiso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, he held visiting roles at Sapienza University of Rome and taught Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~2004).

Francis Whyte Ellis was an Indologist and linguist associated with the East India Company (~1796–1819). He served in the Madras Civil Service, became Deputy Secretary of the Board of Revenue, and founded the College of Fort St. George Press (1812).

Francis Wilford was an Indologist and historian who served in the East India Company military (1781–1794). He was a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1822) and served as Secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Francis William Bain was an Indologist and historian educated at Westminster School, Christ Church, and the University of Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service and was Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College (1892–1919).

Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at Dartmouth and Harvard, he also studied under Paul Pelliot (1935) before serving as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. After studying at Fordham and the University of Chicago, he taught at Boston College (1984–2005) before becoming Parkman Professor of Divinity and comparative theology professor at Harvard in 2005.

Francis Younghusband was an active figure in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Clifton College and the Royal Military College, Sandhurst, and joined the Foreign and Political Department in 1889.

Francisco García Ayuso specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Martin Haug at the University of Munich and held posts at Complutense University of Madrid and Escuela Superior de Comercio de Madrid.

Francisco María Rivero y Godoy was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. from the Complutense University of Madrid in 1866. He subsequently served as the first Professor of Sanskrit at the same university from 1877 to 1881.

Francisco Varela worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and neuroscience. Educated at the University of Chile and Harvard, he studied under Humberto Maturana, Torsten Nils Wiesel, and Chögyam Trungpa, holding posts at CNRS, École Polytechnique, and Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital.

Francisco Xavier de Santa Anna was an Indologist and linguist. He served as a Father in the Order of Discalced Carmelites from 1790 and held the post of Apostolic Vicar in the Archdiocese of Verapoly from 1831 to 1844.
Francisco de Montoliú y Togores was an Indology and religious studies scholar who served as a professor at the Technical University of Madrid. In 1889, he founded the Theosophical Society in Spain.

id: P:Francisco de Paula Canalejas y Casas
summary: Francisco de Paula Canalejas y Casas was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. from Complutense University of Madrid. He was Professor of Literature at the University of Valladolid (1860–1862) and extraordinary professor at Complutense University (~1860–1883).

Franciscus Verellen is a Sinologist and scholar of religion who studied under Kristofer Schipper at EPHE and Oxford. He taught at EPHE and Columbia before serving as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 1991 to 2021.

Franciszek Krček was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Lviv before studying at Charles University under Josef Zubatý, Leipzig, and Berlin. In 1909, he served as a docent at the University of Lviv.

Franciszek Ksawery Malinowski was a Polish linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Warsaw and the Major Seminary of Pelplin, and he became a member of the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences in 1873.

Franciszek Machalski was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Lviv under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak, later working as an assistant there and as an extraordinary professor at Jagiellonian University (1951–1974).

Franciszek Tokarz was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Lviv under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak and at Jagiellonian University under Helena Willman-Grabowska. He later taught Sanskrit at the John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin (1954–1970).
